# v0.3.1 — Messenger scan, browser closing and the CPU monitor, fixed

## Messenger media scan found nothing (now it does)

Three bugs stacked up: modern messengers store media as **hash-named,
extensionless cache blobs** (Telegram `user_data/cache`, Discord
`Cache/Cache_Data`) which the extension-based scan could never match;
**WhatsApp moved to the Store package layout**, which was not mapped; and
**WSL builds could not see Windows messengers** at all. Now:

- Messenger caches follow the browser model: one finding per cache
  directory, purged in place with the same safety guard (messenger roots
  included). Saved media files keep going to the trash.
- The WhatsApp Store package (`5319275A.WhatsAppDesktop_*`) is mapped on
  Windows and WSL.
- The Linux build detects WSL and scans Windows app data through `/mnt/c`.
- The Messenger Media page distinguishes the two flows: caches are
  "deleted permanently, apps rebuild them" (WhatsApp may ask to re-link),
  saved media goes to the trash.

On the machine that reported the bug, the scan went from **0 findings to
36 candidates / 654 MiB**.

## "Close browsers" now really closes browsers

The close button only reached processes with windows; extension and
background processes survived with the cache files still locked, so the
clean still failed. Closing now runs in two phases — graceful close
(WM_CLOSE/SIGTERM), a grace period, then force-termination of the whole
process tree — and the Windows `taskkill` interop handles Windows
browsers from WSL. Exact process names keep Rusty Cleaner's own WebView2
runtime (`msedgewebview2.exe`) out of the kill list, by design and by
test.

## CPU monitor shows real usage

The monitor created a fresh `sysinfo` System on every poll, which has no
delta baseline — sysinfo computes CPU usage between two refreshes — so it
read a constant 100% while the task manager showed ~20%. One System is
now kept alive across polls, turning every reading into a real
measurement.
